extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, Congress, federal science administrators, National Research Foundation planners
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for organizing, staffing, financing, coordinating, and legally supporting governmental and industrial scientific research, including personnel qualifications, recruitment, salaries, tenure, interbureau coordination, advisory bodies, industrial research aids, patent policy, tax treatment of R&D, and international cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational requirements for scientific/professional service entrance
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-establish the requirement of a university or college degree for entrance into all scientific and professional services; exceptions in especially meritorious cases should be granted only upon recommendation of qualified scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to prevent appointments by personal favoritism and political preference and to maintain technical competence in Government scientific services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to lowering standards via special/military preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Any lowering of entrance requirements, whether for civilians or veterans, is distinctly harmful to the scientific services of Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments made through special preference that place unqualified individuals in scientific posts harm the work; such preference is a departure from merit principles and should not reduce standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment practices to attract college talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit government representatives to interview students, reduce months of delay between application, examination, and notification to a few days, and allow college seniors appointments effective on graduation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards can be preserved by longer probationary employment and by requiring suitable examinations before promotion; use of temporary student appointments during summer vacations is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary scales competitive with industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary scales must be broadly commensurate with those of private institutions if scientists are expected to remain in Government service; modify Civil Service to permit exceptionally qualified scientists to reach salaries of $9,000 or more even without administrative duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrance salaries are usually slightly above competitive levels, but promotion is slow and higher positions pay much less than industry; up-grading of positions and salaries plus careful selection would improve government research quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to hire outstanding research directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Although legal restrictions (except need for congressional approval) do not prevent employing directors at necessary salaries, practical considerations (comparisons with other public salaries) limit pay; historically few directors received more than $9,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: War-time exigencies showed higher technical salaries attract talent; permanent up-grading is desirable to retain top leaders in research organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of tenure balanced with performance accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Security of tenure should not become a shelter for incompetence and mediocrity; if scientific/professional personnel are classified separately and receive higher salaries, care must be taken to avoid tenured mediocrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use higher entrance standards, longer and closely supervised probation, examinations for promotions in lowest grades with the alternative of separation, and higher salaries for able scientists to maintain quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interbureau coordination committee/council
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an inter-bureau committee or council of representatives of the principal scientific bureaus (possibly under the Bureau of the Budget) to advise on interrelationships of research programs and compare effectiveness of administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations from such a committee should carry more weight than those of a single bureau; it could advise on budget procedures and classification of scientific personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of scientific employees as cross-bureau consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the practice of utilizing scientific employees of one bureau as consultants for other bureaus to disseminate knowledge of related problems and different methods of attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing regulations make this difficult; general adoption would further coordination of research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous reappraisal and external contact for government research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research projects should be continuously reappraised in light of scientific advance; government employees should maintain close contact with professional colleagues, participate in scientific societies, and have funds for travel to scientific meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orderly revision of programs should be normal; encourage assignments on full pay for graduate work or research at universities, endowed or industrial institutions, and invite visiting scientists including foreigners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify patent policy for government employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign all inventions made within the specifically designated duties of Government employees to the Government; doubtful cases should be decided by a central board on Government patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current patchy patent policies undermine public confidence and industry willingness to share information; centralizing assignments and decisions will improve trust and cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committees for bureaus conducting extensive research
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish advisory committees composed of scientists from outside Government for each bureau or agency with extensive research, since existing committees have proven valuable but are not universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outside advice helps raise performance; committees should be used widely rather than only by progressive bureaus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent Science Advisory Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a permanent Science Advisory Board (similar to the temporary 1933–35 body) empowered to assume overall responsibility for advising branches of Government in scientific matters and to correlate specialized advisory committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board could recommend committee personnel, advise Congress and the Bureau of the Budget on quality and importance of research, and meet at intervals with the interbureau committee; cooperation with the National Research Foundation is suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustaining grants to regional technical clinics for small business
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower the National Research Foundation to make sustaining grants to nonprofit technical clinics that serve small business enterprises, to cover part of administrative costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities should include stimulating business interest in research, helping interpret technical trends, consulting with individual concerns, and maintaining directories to connect small businessmen with competent resources; staff should include general advisors and panels of experts; universities and nonprofit institutes should be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to nonprofit industrial institutes for fundamental research
rubrics_metrics.description: Make nonprofit industrial institutes that are capable of important long-range research eligible for grants for fundamental research from the National Research Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These institutes often face pressure for short-range accomplishments; eligible grants would support sufficiently basic, long-term work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate encouragement methods for new scientific enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge the National Research Foundation to study and devise methods to encourage the launching of small scientific enterprises and to provide opportunities for young engineers/scientists to develop inventions and start enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions include encouraging undergraduates to study unsolved technical problems and providing paths for inventors to complete and commercialize ideas outside the long career ladder of large firms; the Committee could not agree on specific solutions and recommends careful investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen the patent system as essential to research
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize the vital importance of a strong patent system to development of small enterprises and stimulation of healthy scientific research; further study to follow in a separate report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detailed recommendations here, but the Committee urges inquiry and strengthening of patent laws and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal clarity for deductibility of R&D expenditures (Recommendation 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend the Internal Revenue Code to give taxpayers an option each year to (a) deduct currently all expenditures on scientific research and development (other than acquisition of tangible capital assets), or (b) capitalize such expenditures as deferred charges and amortize them under a taxpayer-judged reasonable plan, or (c) deduct that part judged current and capitalize/amortize the remainder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would give clear legal sanction to present Treasury practice, remove uncertainty (particularly harming small/new firms), and give flexibility since no simple universal rule fits all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional amortization for tangible capital assets used for R&D (Recommendation 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend the Code to give taxpayer an option to (a) amortize the cost of tangible capital assets used for R&D in equal amounts over five years, or (b) depreciate such assets at the same rates ordinarily allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides optional accelerated amortization for a small fraction of fixed assets; supported by many businessmen and avoids large revenue impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader tax provisions to aid research
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt broader tax revisions helpful to stimulating R&D: (1) make refunds from carry-back provisions and postwar refund of excess profits taxes more promptly available during transition; (2) increase net operating loss carry-over from 2 years to at least 5 or 6 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures, desirable on other grounds, would particularly help small firms undertaking research by improving cash flow and risk absorption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official support for international cooperative scientific enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge the National Research Foundation to participate in international cooperative scientific enterprises, including modest financing and facilitation of travel and visas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official participation would add value by providing uniform methods, easing logistics, and enabling U.S. involvement in multi-country scientific endeavors (example: International Polar Year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for international scientific congresses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation should participate in arrangements for international scientific conferences to bring workers together and assist with finances and official courtesies for foreign participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. hosts were previously hampered by lack of Government aid and official recognition; Foundation support would alleviate these problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: International fellowships program
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower the Foundation to grant scholarships and fellowships to Americans for foreign travel/study and to foreign scientists to undertake advanced research in the U.S., awarding with care to avoid political/personal interests and drawing on NRC/private foundation experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships promote scientific progress and international understanding; select disinterested representatives and consult experienced organizations for program design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of scientific attachés to embassies (experiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment with appointing scientific attachés of high professional attainment to selected U.S. embassies for temporary tenures (1–2 years) to facilitate scientific cooperation and improve knowledge of foreign scientific practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly valuable in countries where science is government-controlled (e.g., Russia); duties include facilitating travel, cooperation, and informal exchange of scientific information.
